subsystems.name: Sail
subsystems.role: the light-catching surface — a reflective membrane maybe 4 m across but weighing grams, since acceleration comes from having almost no mass.
parts: nanofabricated stiffening ribs and shape control

subsystems.name: Probe payload
subsystems.role: a wafer-scale spacecraft carrying everything needed to observe and report back.

subsystems.name: Laser array
subsystems.role: a ground installation kilometres across whose beams combine into one powerful, steerable pulse.

subsystems.name: Beam pointing and tracking
subsystems.role: keeps the combined beam centred on the sail as it shrinks into the distance.

subsystems.name: Deployment and release mechanism
subsystems.role: folds the sail for launch and releases it cleanly in vacuum.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the sail membrane
buildSteps.detail: A reflective film is deposited onto a sacrificial substrate and patterned at the nanoscale so it stays flat and stiff while weighing almost nothing; the substrate is then etched away. The concept calls for a film hundreds of atoms thick, many times thinner than any sail flown so far.

buildSteps.title: Build the probe
buildSteps.detail: Camera, processor, transmitter and power source are integrated on a wafer-scale board of a few grams, using the same fabrication techniques as microelectronics.

buildSteps.title: Assemble probe and sail
buildSteps.detail: The sail is stowed with the probe at its centre, on a carrier spacecraft that will release it once in vacuum.

buildSteps.title: Build the laser array
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of emitters are phased together so their light adds constructively, with adaptive optics correcting for the atmosphere. Power must reach the gigawatt class, orders of magnitude beyond today's laser installations.

buildSteps.title: Launch and deploy
buildSteps.detail: A conventional rocket carries the carrier to space; the stowed probe separates and the sail unfurls, held by centrifugal spin or lightweight booms.

buildSteps.title: Accelerate
buildSteps.detail: The array fires for a few minutes over a fraction of an astronomical unit, pushing the sail with photon pressure. A perfect reflector feels about 2P/c, so gigawatts across a few square metres can drive a gram-scale probe to tens of thousands of kilometres per second — a large fraction of light speed — within minutes.

buildSteps.title: Coast
buildSteps.detail: The laser cannot follow the probe far; it coasts for years. At 20% of light speed the nearest stars are roughly two decades away.

buildSteps.title: Image and transmit
buildSteps.detail: The probe photographs its target during a flyby lasting hours and sends the data back by laser; the signal takes another four years or so to reach Earth.

prerequisites.why: beam-combining is proven at kilowatt to megawatt scale, but the concept needs gigawatts held on a target for minutes.
IKAROS in 2010 and LightSail 2 in 2019 proved sunlight can push a sail, but their films are thousands of times thicker than what is needed for laser acceleration.
a single chip must combine camera, processor, power and a transmitter that survives interplanetary radiation.
laser links have been demonstrated near Earth; a multi-light-year downlink from a gram-scale transmitter is a different problem.
the entire drive only spends minutes accelerating the sail, so any drift off-beam wastes the shot.

pathway.milestone: solar sails flying in interplanetary space; laser arrays demonstrating beam combining
pathway.unlocks: proof that light pressure can guide and propel spacecraft, at modest speed.

pathway.milestone: a laser-accelerated gram-scale sail reaching kilometres per second in Earth orbit
pathway.unlocks: a working beam-riding demonstration and better sail materials.

pathway.milestone: solar-system probes driven by laser or sunlight at hundreds of kilometres per second
pathway.unlocks: fast access to the outer planets and a test bed for long-duration sails and comms.

pathway.milestone: a gram-scale probe sent toward the nearest star system
pathway.unlocks: the first data from another star — decades after launch, and only if sails, laser arrays and downlinks all improve together.
